Modified assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR): The statement’s baseline remains constructive—vaccinations and policy support underpin strengthening activity and employment, with an accommodative stance and a gradual taper consistent with expectations- and term-premium channels under average-inflation targeting. However, the FSR around this period highlights elevated asset valuations, compressed risk premiums, and heightened risk appetite, along with vulnerabilities in nonbank intermediation and funding markets and sensitivity to interest rate repricing in a low-rate environment. These financial stability vulnerabilities temper the optimism implied by accommodative conditions and reinforce the “risks to the outlook remain” caveat; coupled with the possibility that persistent inflation would ultimately require a stronger policy response consistent with the Taylor principle and the literature’s view that QE has more limited real effects than rates, the net tone is supportive but more cautious than before.
